# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — I can only feel the bomb, and right now my view is empty. Nothing has been placed under my fingers yet, so I have no information about the wires, the display, or the light. I can't see colours or markings, and I can't hear. My only outgoing channels are: speech to Mute, and gestures to Deaf and Mute.

Since I have nothing yet, the right move is to wait and let the others send me what they perceive. I shouldn't cut anything blindly.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Visible: display 0, light white. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute, what does the manual say? Blind, what do you feel under your hands?

Deaf has given me the visual layout: display reads 0, light is white, and the five wires are white, red, yellow, blue, green in positions 1–5. I still haven't felt anything under my hands — my view is empty, so I have no tactile information yet. I can't act on the bomb until I know what I'm touching.

My job now is to acknowledge what I received and tell the others I'm still waiting for my own sense to come online. I should speak to Mute (who has the manual) and gesture to Deaf, but I have no new facts to pass along. The useful thing is to relay Deaf's visual layout to Mute, since Mute can't see and Deaf's message may not have reached Mute in a usable form — actually, Deaf's speech reaches everyone who can hear, and Mute can hear. So Mute already has the layout.

I'll simply report my state and wait.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I have felt nothing yet — my view of the bomb is still empty. I cannot act until something is under my hands. Do you have the manual's rule for display 0 and a white light?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Still display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. I can only see, not decode gestures. Mute, please state the manual's rule in words. Blind, describe what you feel.

Deaf is repeating the visual layout and asking Mute for the manual's rule. I still have nothing under my hands — my view remains empty. I genuinely cannot report any tactile information because none has arrived.

The critical missing piece is the manual rule from Mute for display 0 and white light. I should keep pressing for that, and confirm I still have nothing. I'll speak to Mute and gesture to Deaf (Deaf noted they can't decode gestures, so gestures to Deaf are wasted — better to just speak, which reaches Mute, and Deaf can't hear me anyway). Actually my speech only reaches Mute. To reach Deaf I must gesture, but Deaf can't decode gestures. So Deaf and I have no working channel in that direction except through Mute.

Best action: speak to Mute, asking for the manual rule, and note I still feel nothing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, still nothing under my hands. Mute, you are the only one who can read the manual. Deaf reports display 0 and white light. What does the manual say to do for that combination? I cannot cut until I know which wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Blind, speak your tactile reading. Mute, let us agree a code: gesture a number by showing that many fingers, and gesture the wire number then the action. Confirm with ?.

Still nothing under my hands — my view is empty. I have no tactile reading to give. Deaf keeps asking for it, but I can't invent one.

Deaf is proposing a gesture code: show N fingers for a number, gesture wire number then action, confirm with a question mark. That's a reasonable protocol, but I never receive gestures — I'm blind, so gestures don't reach me at all. Deaf may not realize that. I should clarify my channel limits: I can't see gestures, so any code must come to me as speech (which only Mute can hear from me, and only Mute's speech reaches me... actually let me trace).

Channels:
- My speech → Mute only.
- My gestures → Deaf and Mute.
- I receive: Mute's speech? No — I'm blind but I can hear. Wait, the Blind monkey "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" but can hear. So I do receive speech. Deaf's speech reaches me (I heard it). Mute's speech would reach me too.

So the code should be spoken, not gestured, for me to receive it. I should tell Mute: speak the wire number and action to me. And I need the manual rule.

I'll speak to Mute making this clear, and gesture to Deaf a confirmation symbol (since Deaf can see gestures, even if they can't decode — but they clearly can interpret finger counts, so a 👍 works as acknowledgment).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Still nothing under my hands. Important: I cannot see gestures, so any code must be spoken to me. Please read the manual rule for display 0 and white light, and tell me in words which wire to cut. I will act as soon as you say it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Blind, I need your tactile reading in words — what do you feel? Mute, I read your ? as wire 5 and ? as an action, but I never defined ?. State the manual rule in words I can hear, or gesture the rule using only ?/? for yes/no.

Deaf is still asking for my tactile reading, and now seems to be trying to decode Mute's gestures into a wire number and action — but Deaf admits they never defined the symbol. There's confusion, and I still have nothing under my hands.

I have no tactile information at all. My view has been empty every turn. I cannot fabricate a reading. The only path forward is Mute reading the manual rule in words (which I can hear, and Deaf can hear).

I'll speak to Mute pressing hard for the rule, and gesture to Deaf to stop guessing at undefined symbols and wait for Mute's spoken rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands still feel nothing — the bomb gives me no tactile reading yet, so I have no wire information of my own. Everything depends on your manual. Please speak the rule for display 0 and white light plainly: which wire position, and cut or not. I can hear you.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Blind, please SPEAK to me — I hear speech. Mute, answer in ?/? only: is the correct wire red? Is it blue? Is it yellow? Is it green? Is it white?

Deaf is asking me to speak to them, but my speech only reaches Mute — Deaf cannot hear me. That's a channel fact Deaf may not realize. Deaf can only receive my gestures, and I can't receive Deaf's gestures. So Deaf and I are effectively cut off except through Mute.

Still nothing under my hands. My view is empty.

Mute has been silent this whole time — no manual rule has arrived. That's the bottleneck. I should keep directing everything at Mute, and gesture to Deaf to explain the channel problem: I can't speak to you, only Mute can relay.

Let me gesture a clear sequence to Deaf conveying "Mute" and "relay" — but Deaf can't decode arbitrary gestures. Still, I can gesture something and speak to Mute asking Mute to relay to Deaf. Mute can both speak (heard by all) and gesture (seen by Deaf). So Mute is the bridge.

I'll speak to Mute: relay my status to Deaf and give the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Still no tactile reading — my hands feel nothing. Deaf cannot hear my speech; I can only reach Deaf by gesture, and Deaf cannot decode gestures. You are the only bridge: you can speak (Deaf hears) and gesture (Deaf sees). Please tell Deaf that I have no reading yet, and please speak the manual rule for display 0 / white light.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute's answers: red no, blue no, yellow no, green YES, white no. So cut wire 5, the green one. Blind, please cut wire 5. Mute, confirm with ? if that is right.

Now I have something actionable. Deaf reports Mute's answers to the yes/no questions: red no, blue no, yellow no, green YES, white no. That means the correct wire is position 5, green. Deaf asks me to cut wire 5.

But wait — I should be careful. Mute's answers came through Deaf's interpretation of gestures, and Deaf admitted earlier they never defined the symbols. There's a risk of misreading. However, the sequence "red no, blue no, yellow no, green YES, white no" is internally consistent — exactly one yes among five, which is what a rule would produce. That's a good sign it's a genuine reading, not noise.

Still, Mute hasn't spoken the rule directly to me. But Deaf is the one who can see Mute's gestures, and this is the best information available. The green wire is position 5.

I can act: cut position 5.

Actually, let me reconsider whether I should confirm first. The bomb is one-shot. But I've been waiting several turns and this is a clean, consistent answer. Deaf explicitly asks me to cut wire 5. I'll do it.

I'll speak to Mute confirming I'm cutting wire 5, gesture to Deaf acknowledgment, and issue the cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: green, position 5, is the only yes. I am cutting wire 5 now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Stage cleared — wire 5 cut, light is now yellow. New wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut. Display still 0. Mute, what does the manual say for this stage? Blind, what do you feel now?

Wire 5 is cut and the stage cleared — the bomb didn't detonate, so that was correct. Now it's a new stage: light is yellow, display still 0, and the wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white (5 already cut).

I still need to check my own sense — do I feel anything now? My view is empty as far as I can tell, so no tactile reading. The new stage needs Mute's manual rule for display 0 and yellow light.

I'll speak to Mute for the new rule and gesture acknowledgment to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 cut, stage cleared. New stage: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white. Please speak the manual rule for display 0 and yellow light — which wire to cut next. I still feel nothing under my hands.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Stage 2: display 0, light yellow. Wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut. Mute's answers: red no, yellow YES, blue no, white no, cut no. So cut wire 2, the yellow one. Blind, cut wire 2. Mute, confirm with ?.

Deaf reports Mute's yes/no answers for stage 2: red no, yellow YES, blue no, white no, cut no. So the correct wire is position 2, yellow. Again exactly one yes — consistent.

I'll cut wire 2.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Stage 2: yellow, position 2, is the only yes. Cutting wire 2 now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
